reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about mixing enthalpy, bonding strength, and melting behavior in high-entropy alloy nanoparticles, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the quantitative link between mixing enthalpy and nanoparticle premelting, so the lack of citations leaves all key premises unsupported.
premises: Mixing enthalpy can be systematically varied by slight compositional changes while preserving high-entropy character and particle size
More negative mixing enthalpy corresponds to stronger interatomic bonding in high-entropy alloy nanoparticles
Stronger interatomic bonding increases the energy barrier for atom mobility, delaying premelting and raising melting temperature
Configurational entropy favors a homogeneous phase and competes with enthalpy-driven segregation or stabilization
The enthalpy–entropy competition governs premelting and melting behavior across the 5–20 nm size range
